events.title: The canonization of John XXIII and John Paul II
events.shortBlurb: On Divine Mercy Sunday, two twentieth-century popes were declared saints together…
body: On 27 April 2014, Divine Mercy Sunday, Pope Francis canonized two of his predecessors, John XXIII and John Paul II, before an immense crowd in St. Peter's Square. The retired Pope Benedict XVI was present, a striking gathering of living and departed popes.

John XXIII, who reigned from 1958 to 1963, had summoned the Second Vatican Council and was beloved as “the Good Pope.” John Paul II, who reigned from 1978 to 2005, had guided the Church for more than a quarter-century and was raised to the altars only nine years after his death.
The rare double canonization was seen as a symbol of continuity across the era of the council and the decades that followed it.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of Sts. John XXIII and John Paul II (vatican.va)
